one_month_reasoning: Unchanged from round 1, which the supervisor confirmed. AMD has not announced its Q3 2026 date; Nov 3 is an aggregator estimate (MarketBeat). Past Q3 prints were Oct 26 2021, Nov 1 2022, Oct 31 2023, Oct 29 2024 and Nov 4 2025, so 2 of 5 would fall inside an Oct-30 cutoff; I keep ~25-30% odds of an in-window print. In-window events: the Oct 27-28 FOMC after the Sep 16 hike (a second hike priced ~56-69% on Kalshi/Polymarket as of Sep 29) and late-October hyperscaler capex guides. The stock just ran ~25% in five sessions to a $1T cap near its $639 high. Net: median ~$600, monthly sigma ~18% (between the 72%/3.5 rule and calmer forward vol), a touch fatter on the downside.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a slow MI450/Helios rack ramp (pace risk, not the stale Feb-2026 delay report), together with a Fed hiking cycle and a 35% Polymarket chance of recession by end-2027. FY28 EPS is cut to ~$17-18, the multiple falls to ~19x on a diluted share count, a typical AMD post-peak de-rating (past drawdowns of 60-90%).

base.story: Data center roughly doubles in 2027 as guided and Helios ramps from late Q3 2026 with step-ups in Q4 and Q1'27; EPS tracks consensus ($15.58 FY27, ~$20 NTM), but the multiple compresses from ~39x to ~30x and ~4.5% dilution lands, so the price is roughly flat after a +281% year.

bull.story: MI450/MI500 take meaningful share from Nvidia and the OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic gigawatt deployments run ahead of schedule; FY28 EPS moves toward $28-30 and the multiple holds at ~33x, net of warrant dilution (which vests faster in this case).

thesis_break_reason: Kept at ~$420 (supervisor used $400). At ~$420 AMD would trade at ~27x FY27 consensus ($15.58) and ~20x a ~$21.5 FY28 path on a diluted basis, and below the June 2026 selloff low (~$466). A 30% fall is only ~0.5 sigma at 72% vol, so I set the level at a valuation breakpoint: trading there would most likely mean the market no longer believes the guided 2027 data-center doubling (a real Helios/MI450 ramp slip beyond Q1'27, a cut to the first-GW commitments of OpenAI, Meta or Anthropic, a hyperscaler 2027 capex reset, or export/tariff damage). I keep $420 rather than $400 because the June low is the more relevant base-rate marker for a failed breakout.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks changed three inputs. (1) My EV/sales leg at 7.5x implied ~21x my own NTM earnings, inconsistent with my 30x P/E leg; I re-based it to 10x (~28.5x earnings, a small margin-risk haircut), raising that leg from $435 to $553, and cut its weight to 25% since it is now largely a cross-check. (2) I had no dilution; the 10-Q shows no warrant tranches vested at June 27, so ~40-70M expected warrant shares plus ~13.6M World Labs shares (~4.5%) are outside consensus EPS; I apply it to both legs. (3) FY27 consensus is $15.58 (Yahoo, 50 analysts); my FY28 figure is now flagged as derived and set at ~$21.5 (aggregators ~$19-22.8, the forward-P/E-implied $22.4, and management's 'significantly exceed $20'). Fair value rises from $550 to ~$573, still ~5% below spot. I stay slightly below the supervisor's $580 because the base-rate evidence (stocks that triple rarely repeat; AMD's repeated 60-90% post-peak drawdowns; a Fed hiking cycle with 35% recession odds on Polymarket for end-2027) argues for a modest haircut to a pure 30x-consensus value. Base rates still anchor the distribution: 72% realized vol, a small positive momentum drift that is not significant for large caps after beta, and a fat left tail. Scenarios ($340/25%, $610/50%, $960/25%) give a mean of ~$630; the ladder is a lognormal with median ~$597 and sigma ~0.55 with a fattened left tail, which is ~1-1.5pp above round 1 near the money. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research this round was one search on the Q3 date (still unconfirmed by AMD), one on FY28 consensus and one data-page fetch (StockAnalysis hides FY27/28 estimates behind a paywall).
